items.title: Nvidia's model GR00T 2 watches humans on video, then imagines itself as the robot
items.content_text: To teach robots new tasks, humans usually have to laboriously teleoperate them during training. Nvidia's new AI model GR00T 2 is designed to cut that effort by transferring human movements from videos to robotic arms. To train a robot for new tasks, engineers usually spend hours remotely controlling the machines. This so-called teleoperation is expensive, slow, and needs its own data for every robot model. items.title: Alta, which is building blockchain infrastructure for banks and payment companies, raised a $47.5M Series A, bringing its total funding to $80M (Kyle Baird/The Block)
items.content_text: Alta, a blockchain infrastructure provider for banks and payment firms, raised $47.5 million in Series A funding led by Index Ventures. Bringing its total funding to $80 million, the company aims to modernize payment and settlement rails for traditional financial institutions.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon arrives just in time to feel like yesterday's news in the fastest model cycle yet
items.content_text: Google has released Gemini 4 Carbon, a model designed for complex multi-step coding and scientific research, positioning it as a deeper reasoning companion to Argon. However, the model is already losing its luster as Anthropic’s new Fable 5.2 model outperforms it in benchmarks, highlighting an increasingly brutal pace of AI model iteration.

items.title: The AI Futures Project updates its AI timelines after METR's report on Anthropic R&D, saying it now expects a Superhuman AI Researcher to arrive in 2027 (AI Futures Project)
items.content_text: The AI Futures Project, citing METR's report on Anthropic's R&D pace, has updated its forecast, predicting the arrival of a 'Superhuman AI Researcher' by 2027. The report notes that AI development is currently progressing twice as fast as historical trends, with AI itself driving roughly 80% of this acceleration.

items.title: Oura agrees to acquire AI and on-demand doctor service Counsel Health for $625M, says Q4 revenue grew 153% YoY to $533M and FY 2026 revenue grew 92% to $1.75B (Mark Gurman/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Smart ring manufacturer Oura has agreed to acquire the AI-driven on-demand doctor service platform Counsel Health for $625 million. This acquisition aims to bolster Oura's medical diagnostic capabilities beyond mere data tracking, backed by a strong financial performance of 153% YoY growth in Q4 and a 92% increase in total 2026 revenue.

items.title: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 scores 96 percent sorting metal parts in a Mercedes-Benz assembly pilot
items.content_text: Google DeepMind unveiled the Gemini 2.5 robotic model, integrating vision, language, and motion control to operate diverse hardware like Apptronik robots. In pilot tests at Mercedes-Benz plants, the model achieved a 96% success rate and increased task speed by up to 30%.

items.title: Dreeze, launched by Zerto founders to help companies recover from cyberattacks by restoring entire cloud applications, emerges from stealth with a $33M seed (CTech)
items.content_text: Founded by the Zerto team, Dreeze emerged from stealth with $33 million in seed funding. The company focuses on recovering entire cloud applications, including infrastructure and configurations, rather than just data, to ensure business continuity after cyberattacks.

items.title: Updated S-1: Anthropic's seven co-founders will sell $1.75B of stock in next week's IPO, each offering shares worth ~$250M at the midpoint of its IPO range (Dylan Sloan/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Anthropic revealed in an updated S-1 filing that its seven co-founders plan to sell $1.75 billion worth of stock during next week's IPO. This move allows the founders to cash out, with each taking home approximately $250 million at the offering's midpoint.

items.title: Reddit launches Reddit Reviews, a built-in hub using AI to turn subreddit comments into product pages with pros, cons, and sentiment, starting with 10K items (Mia Sato/The Verge)
items.content_text: Reddit launched a product review hub that uses AI to analyze and summarize millions of subreddit discussions into structured product pages covering 10,000 items. This initiative aims to monetize the platform's reputation for authentic user recommendations while challenging traditional review outlets.

items.title: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 completes 41 percent of real freelance jobs, up from 2.5 percent a year ago
items.content_text: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 model has achieved a 41.3% success rate on the Remote Labor Index, completing professional freelance projects at a standard acceptable to paying clients. This represents a 16-fold increase in capability since the benchmark's inception a year ago, signaling a massive leap in agentic productivity.

items.title: Anthropic targets $1.4 trillion IPO
items.content_text: Anthropic has confirmed its upcoming IPO, planning to list on the Nasdaq with shares priced between $70 and $78. While falling short of the most ambitious $2 trillion valuation rumors, the move signals a major milestone in the AI sector's public market debut race.
